definitions.explanation: A gymnastics apparatus consisting of a single bar supported by two posts, used for swinging and acrobatic exercises. Also refers to the horizontal bar commonly found in school playgrounds in Japan.
A bar or rod made of iron, used as a tool or weapon.

examples.japanese: {鉄棒|てつぼう}で{逆上|さかあ}がりをする。
examples.english: To do a pull-over on the horizontal bar.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちが{校庭|こうてい}の{鉄棒|てつぼう}で{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The children are playing on the horizontal bar in the schoolyard.

examples.japanese: {体操|たいそう}{選手|せんしゅ}が{鉄棒|てつぼう}で{見事|みごと}な{演技|えんぎ}を{披露|ひろう}した。
examples.english: The gymnast performed a splendid routine on the horizontal bar.

examples.japanese: {鉄棒|てつぼう}で{殴|なぐ}られた。
examples.english: I was hit with an iron bar.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}は{鉄棒|てつぼう}を{手|て}にしていた。
examples.english: The criminal was holding an iron bar.

examples.japanese: {工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}に{太|ふと}い{鉄棒|てつぼう}が{何本|なんぼん}も{積|つ}まれていた。
examples.english: Thick iron bars were piled up at the construction site.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 is more common in everyday speech, especially in the context of school and gymnastics. In Japanese schools, the {鉄棒|てつぼう} is standard playground equipment, and {逆上|さかあ}がり (pull-over) is a common exercise children learn.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄棒|てつぼう}で{遊|あそ}ぶ (to play on the horizontal bar)
- {鉄棒|てつぼう}の{演技|えんぎ} (horizontal bar routine)
- {逆上|さかあ}がり (pull-over on the bar)
